title: hardening-1 Gates prove the built image

goal.statement: The test service runs the built image with OWNER_EMAIL forwarded (default owner@example.com) and no bind mounts, build_check.sh has no unused loop variable, and docs/STANDARDS.md is registered as standards knowledge.

title: hardening-2 Unreadable email files are Skipped Files

goal.statement: The Mailbox lower-cases Senders once, matches .EML/.PDF case-insensitively, reads HTML-only Messages, and counts every unreadable, undecodable or undated file as a Skipped File with only specific parse errors caught.

title: hardening-3 Wrapped headers and whole Action Items

goal.statement: A PDF Email's unindented wrapped header value continues its header, a repeated header keeps its first value, and Action Item sentences are not split at decimals or common abbreviations.

title: hardening-4 The Digest Day is a strict day

goal.statement: The web interface speaks of day (with ?date= as alias), returns 400 for an empty, malformed or unpadded day, renders the first and last representable days without a link beyond them, and shows the sample Mailbox's Needs Reply for the default Owner.

title: hardening-5 The page is readable and errors are logged

goal.statement: The page carries a viewport meta tag, inline stylesheet, visible EML/PDF badge and 'No mail on this day' for a quiet day, request errors are logged, and the by-eye readability is left to the reviewer.

title: hardening-6 Bytecode is not committed

goal.statement: The committed app/__pycache__/*.pyc files are removed from git and a root .gitignore keeps bytecode, caches and machine-local files out.

title: hardening-7 The web service forwards the Owner

goal.statement: The web service forwards OWNER_EMAIL with the default owner@example.com exactly as test does, proved by a check build_check.sh runs.

title: hardening-8 build_digest returns the day key

goal.statement: build_digest itself returns the Digest Day under the key day, with its unit tests updated, and server.py no longer renames it.

title: hardening-9 A wrapped last header stays in its header

goal.statement: A PDF Email header value that wraps onto an unindented line after the last header line continues that header instead of spilling into the body.

title: hardening-10 The blank line ends the Header Block

goal.statement: In a PDF Email, an unindented line that is not a header continues the last header while the body has not started (no blank line yet), and an unparseable Date no longer absorbs a following header or body line.
